newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha prices ease in subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha prices ease in subdued trade.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices eased on Friday, reflecting softer crude prices while end-users kept to the sidelines seeing ample prompt supplies, traders said.
News of Mobil Singapore closing its 45,000 barrels-per-day crude unit earlier this week owning to technical problems had little impact on the market, traders said.

Open-spec naphtha second-half March was assessed at $230.00/232.00 and first-half April at $229.00/231.00, against Thursday levels of $231.00/233.00 and $230.50/232.00 respectively. The one-month spread from second-half March was at $2.00/3.00 against $1.50/3.00 on Thursday.
The backwardation is expected to stabilise at levels of about $3.00 to $4.00, a trader said.
Physical buying for second-half February seems to have been completed and potential buyers of first-half March seem to be relaxed as supplies are sufficient, traders said.

Traders said news on Thursday of Taiwan's CPC cutting output of one of its naphtha crackers with annual capacity of 385,000 tonnes of ethylene by about 10 percent to reduce inventories also failed to effect market sentiment.
"Small-scale cuts do not seem to have an impact on the market at the moment," a second trader said.
